---
title: "Glossary"
---

Short definitions of terms used across ARCS, with links back to where each one is taught and out to fuller references.

### Argument {#argument}
A value passed into a function when it is called — the function's input.
→ [Arc 1](/modules/arc_1.qmd#calling-functions) · [Advanced R: Functions](http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Functions.html)

### Assignment Operator {#assignment-operator}
`<-`, used to store a value in an object. Read it as "gets" — `x <- 5` means "x gets 5."
→ [Arc 1](/modules/arc_1.qmd#objects-and-assignment)

### Commit {#commit}
A saved snapshot of a project's files at a specific point in time, created in git with a short message describing what changed and why.
→ [Arc 6](/modules/arc_6.qmd#local-git-in-positron-modify-stage-commit)

### Data Frame {#data-frame}
A table-like object in R — rows and columns, similar to a spreadsheet.
→ [Arc 1](/modules/arc_1.qmd#building-your-first-data-frame) · [R for Data Science: Data Frames](https://r4ds.hadley.nz)

### Data Repository {#data-repository}
A system designed for depositing, preserving, and sharing research data long-term — distinct from a code repository like GitHub, which is built for tracking changes to text and scripts, not hosting datasets. Examples include Zenodo, Dryad, and institutional repositories.
→ [Arc 6](/modules/arc_6.qmd#excluding-data-files-the-gitignore-file) · [Arc 8](/modules/arc_8.qmd)

### Data Type {#data-type}
The kind of value an object holds — `numeric`, `character`, or `logical`. Determines what operations R will let you perform on it.
→ [Arc 1](/modules/arc_1.qmd#data-types) · [R Language Definition](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-lang.html#Basic-types)

### Function {#function}
A reusable block of code that takes arguments (inputs) and returns a value (output).
→ [Arc 1](/modules/arc_1.qmd#calling-functions) · [Advanced R: Functions](http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Functions.html)

### .gitignore {#gitignore}
A plain-text file in a project's root folder listing files and folders git should never track — typically large data files, output files, and package caches.
→ [Arc 6](/modules/arc_6.qmd#excluding-data-files-the-gitignore-file) · [GitHub: .gitignore docs](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/getting-started-with-git/ignoring-files)

### IDE
IDE stands for "integrated development environment", a kind of software application that combines a variety of developer tools together into one interface, as opposed to many narrower standalone applications. Positron, R Studio, and VS Code are examples of IDEs. 
→ [Arc 0](/modules/arc_0.qmd) · [GitHub: What is an IDE?](https://github.com/resources/articles/what-is-an-ide)

### Object {#object}
A named value stored in R's environment, created with the assignment operator `<-`.
→ [Arc 1](/modules/arc_1.qmd#objects-and-assignment)

### Package {#package}
A bundle of R functions, data, and documentation that extends what base R can do — installed once with `install.packages()` and loaded per session with `library()`.
→ [Arc 2](/modules/arc_2.qmd#what-is-a-package) · [Arc 5](/modules/arc_5.qmd) · [R Packages, 2nd ed.](https://r-pkgs.org/)

### R Project {#r-project}
A folder that Positron/RStudio treats as a self-contained working directory, keeping file paths and settings local to that project rather than scattered across your computer.
→ [Arc 2](/modules/arc_2.qmd#create-an-r-project)

### Repository {#repository}
In git, a project folder tracked for version history — distinct from a [data repository](#data-repository), which is built for depositing and sharing datasets that represent scientific findings, often governed by human curation.
→ [Arc 6](/modules/arc_6.qmd#checking-whether-git-is-initialized) · [Arc 8](/modules/arc_8.qmd)

### README {#readme}
A plain-text file describing what a project contains and how to use it, so a collaborator — or future you — doesn't have to guess.
→ [Arc 2](/modules/arc_2.qmd#write-a-readme) · [Cornell README Template](https://ecommons.cornell.edu/entities/publication/6effe964-798e-4c21-aac2-4194709ff230)

### renv {#renv}
An R package that locks the exact version of every package a project uses, so the project runs identically on any machine, including yours a year from now.
→ [Arc 2](/modules/arc_2.qmd#initialize-renv) · [renv documentation](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/)

### Reproducibility {#reproducibility}
The property of a project, script, or pipeline producing the same result every time it's re-run — including after changes to upstream data, parameters, or package versions.
→ [Arc 1: Code Tour](/modules/arc_1.qmd#objects-and-assignment) · [Arc 2](/modules/arc_2.qmd#why-project-management-matters) · [The Turing Way: Definitions](https://book.the-turing-way.org/reproducible-research/overview/overview-definitions/#rr-overview-definitions-reproducibility)

### Vector {#vector}
A collection of values of the same data type, created with `c()`.
→ [Arc 1](/modules/arc_1.qmd#vectors)

### Working Directory {#working-directory}
The folder R treats as "home" for a session — where it looks for files by default, and where relative file paths are measured from.
→ [Arc 1](/modules/arc_1.qmd#orient-to-positron)
